modern: Socrates excused himself to Perdiccas for not going to him, saying: It is because I do not want to perish by the worst of all ends; that is, I do not want to receive a favour and then be unable to return it.
original: Socrates excused himself to Perdiccas for not going to him, saying, It is because I would not perish by the worst of all ends; that is, I would not receive a favor and then be unable to return it.

explained.summary: Socrates declined an invitation from a Macedonian king, explaining that he didn’t want to die the worst death of all: receiving favours he could never repay. It’s a pointed story about independence. Accepting too much from the powerful puts you in their debt, and Socrates preferred to stay free.
explained.today: It’s the same instinct that makes someone turn down lavish gifts from a client or an expensive trip from a supplier. Once you owe someone more than you can return, it gets harder to say no to them or to speak your mind.
